text:
mara: Seeing a spike of support tickets — users can't sign in via SSO since ~15:02 UTC. Error in the client logs is `invalid_client` and `client_assertion expired` when we hit the OIDC token endpoint. Noticed a SCIM sync also failed around the same time and a few org admins are now missing org-admin role.

idp-bot: SSO config change detected for idp-okta-prod by ops@okta at 2026-03-20T15:01:18Z :rotating_light: 

jonathan: Oof. Likely JWKS/key rollover on the IdP side. Two things to check quickly: 1) our OIDC client assertion signing `kid` matches the IdP JWKS, 2) the `exp` on the client_assertion isn't being set incorrectly (some libs default to a very short TTL).

alice: Also confirm the token endpoint response body — sometimes IdP returns `invalid_client` when the `client_id` in the assertion `sub`/`iss` mismatch.

mara: Here's the token error we captured (redacted):
```
POST /oauth2/v1/token HTTP/1.1
Host: login.example-idp.com
grant_type=client_credentials&client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer
{
  "error": "invalid_client",
  "error_description": "client_assertion has expired"
}
```

eli: Can someone run a quick JWKS fetch? `curl -s https://login.example-idp.com/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'`

jonathan: I pulled the JWKS — new `kid` present: `"kid": "rk-2026-03-20-14"` and there's an older one `"kid": "rk-2025-11-01-01"` that we expected. Our signing lib defaulted to using the old kid.

mara: That would explain token rejects. But why did SCIM fail and demote admins? SCIM sync returned 403 for group PATCH at 15:02:32.

alice: If the OIDC auth used for the SCIM app failed, the SCIM client couldn't call the provisioning API — resulting in partial sync. For group-to-role mapping, our runtime applies mapping during provisioning push; missing updates can remove transient role assignments.

jonathan: Steps I'd take: 1) rotate our client key to use new `kid` and sign assertions with RS256, 2) resend the SCIM delta for affected orgs, 3) check audit log encryption pipeline (mara mentioned some audit logs are missing for 15:00-15:10 window).

mara: Quick note — KMS rotation happened yesterday morning for the audit pipeline; we saw one key version marked `PendingDeletion` but we thought audit ingestion had a fallback. Could KMS rotation + re-encryption delay have dropped logs?

eli: If the audit producer failed to encrypt payloads (error 500) and our ingestion pipeline discards failed writes, that would explain gaps. Check producer logs `/var/log/audit-producer/audit.log` around 15:00.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03120-7 — "SSO auth + SCIM sync failures". Pager severity P2.

jonathan: Recovery plan then: 1) revert signing to previous active key while we update client config (hotfix). 2) Trigger SCIM full resync for affected orgs. 3) Backfill audit logs if producer retries are available; if not, mark gaps. 4) Patch signing lib to prefer `kid` selection from latest JWKS and fail open with informative logs.

alice: For backfill: if audit producer has the raw queue (S3 staging), we can re-run the encrypt->ingest job after pointing it to the new KMS key alias. If raw payloads were not persisted, we'll have to treat as lost and mention in incident notes.

mara: I'm doing step 1 now: switching client assertion generator to use `rk-2026-03-20-14` and reissuing a signed assertion. Doing a curl test to token endpoint...

mara: Test result: 200 OK, received `access_token` and `expires_in: 3600`. SCIM client call now returns 204 for group PATCH. :white_check_mark:

jonathan: Nice. Once SCIM resync completes, we should verify RBAC state: list org admins for 3 orgs that reported issues and compare to pre-incident snapshot. Run `scripts/roles/compare --org-id <org>` (I pushed a helper earlier).

eli: KMS audit pipeline: producer logs show transient encryption errors from 14:59:51 to 15:04:10 — root cause was the KMS alias pointing to a key scheduled for reimport. I patched alias to the new key and restarted producer; it successfully re-enqueued 87% of pending messages from local disk. The rest were not persisted.

mara: I'm spinning up a SCIM backfill for the affected orgs now. ETA ~8m.

sre-bot: SCIM backfill job scim-backfill-2026-03-20-15:10 finished: 3/3 orgs success.

alice: RBAC comparison: org-a and org-c restored to expected admin sets. org-b had two external users removed permanently (no persisted SCIM delta). We need to manually re-invite them and document in incident notes.

jonathan: Action items for postmortem:
- vendor-idp: confirm key rollover procedure and request advanced notice / JWKS notification hook
- infra: make client JWT builder prefer explicit `kid` mapping and add a health check that validates client_assertion before deploy
- security: update incident runbook to include KMS alias verification steps for audit pipeline
- devex: improve error messages surfaced to support tickets (more actionable: "client_assertion kid mismatch / expired")

mara: I'll draft the incident timeline and put in postmortems/INC-2026-03120-7. Also adding links to logs and commands used.

eli: For immediate guardrails, can we add a small check in our deploy pipeline that fetches IdP JWKS and ensures our chosen `kid` exists? Could be a 1-min preflight script.

jonathan: Yes — I'll open a PR with that preflight check and a fallback to fail the deploy if assertion signing config is stale.

mara: Closing notes: root cause = IdP key rollover + our client_assertion code defaulting to old kid + simultaneous KMS alias rotation exposing gaps in audit persistence. Impact: SSO failures ~8 minutes, SCIM gaps for some orgs, 2 users lost requiring manual re-invite, partial audit log loss for ~4 minutes.

alice: Thanks all — good catch and fast remediation. I'll update the security ticket with remediation status and assign follow-ups.

mara: If anyone runs into more SSO errors after this, ping #eng-security + @oncall. :handshake:
